source.prompt: Instrumental background music for a classic 1990s-style Japanese fantasy role-playing game. The writing and orchestration evoke the golden age of 16-bit console RPG soundtracks (memorable singable lead melody, clear bass line, warm chords, tasteful hall reverb), but the production is high quality, warm and full, recorded with real-sounding instruments. Completely original melody. The game's world lives in an endless night lit by lanterns, lamps and great beacon fires; the score is gentle and melancholic, with warmth and a quiet, stubborn hope. Climbing a dark lighthouse tower whose lamp has gone out: rising spiral stairs, gears and old brass, the sea wind outside. Mysterious and determined, a sense of climbing toward a light that must be rekindled. Tempo 108 BPM, 4/4 time, key of B minor. Instrumentation: climbing celesta and harp arpeggios, violin melody, cello counter-line, ticking woodblock and rim clicks, pizzicato strings, soft pads, low tom accents. Form: ticking intro; climbing theme on violin; a suspended middle where the cello takes the melody; a building passage with tom accents; return to the climbing theme. Duration: 115 seconds. Instrumental only: no vocals, no singing, no spoken words, no lyrics. Keep one steady tempo and key from start to finish, no fade-in and no fade-out, no long silences; the last bar leads naturally back into the first bar so the piece loops seamlessly as game background music.
